subject: AWS Private Offer: pricing bands & term routing for Hyperscale Analytics
messages:
From: Sara Benitez <sara.benitez@hyperscale.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@hyperscale.com>, AWS Partner Manager <am-partner@amazon.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing discovery / private offer path

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the demo earlier. Hyperscale is excited to move toward procurement, but our Legal & Procurement teams prefer a Private Offer on AWS Marketplace for visibility into invoicing and to use our existing PO process. Two quick asks from Procurement:

- Can you confirm pricing for 12-month vs 36-month terms (list price + proposed Redwood discount)?
- What approvals does Hyperscale need internally (CFO signoff vs procurement lead)? We need to map internal owners.

We also want to understand whether Redwood has any minimum commitment or seat-count constraints on Marketplace SKUs, and how renewals are handled if we select a 3-year term.

If we can get a short matrix (term / discount / billing cadence / approval owners), procurement can prepare the buyer-side approval flow. Can you loop in Partner Ops if needed?

Appreciate it — I’ll include procurement in replies.

Best,
Sara Benitez
Head of Infrastructure Procurement
Hyperscale Analytics
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Benitez <sara.benitez@hyperscale.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@hyperscale.com>, AWS Partner Manager <am-partner@amazon.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T10:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing discovery / private offer path

Sara —

Thanks, and great questions. Short answers up front, and a proposed next step below.

Summary (high level):
- Term options: 12m, 24m, 36m supported via AWS Private Offer. Renewals can be auto-renewed or opt-in at expiry; we recommend a 12-month renewal cadence for predictability unless you want price protection for 36 months.
- Pricing: attach is a starter matrix. Proposed discounts: 10% (12m), 18% (24m), 25% (36m) off list for committed annual spend tiers. Discounts are configurable depending on committed token/usage bands.
- Approvals: Typical Hyperscale flow we’ve seen = Procurement review -> Legal review -> CFO signoff for spend > $500k ARR. AWS private offers require the buyer to accept the offer in Marketplace; Procurement usually sends a PO referencing the Marketplace transaction.

I’ve attached a PO template and a short pricing matrix to get Procurement moving (PO_Template_Hyperscale.pdf). Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm anticipated 12/24/36 month committed spend band (monthly avg).
2) We prepare an AWS Private Offer draft and route to your Procurement + Legal for signature.
3) Loop in AM to push the Private Offer through AWS console (we’ll need offer metadata + buyer AWS account id).

If helpful, I can propose a short routing/owner checklist for your team to speed up internal approvals. Would you prefer a single combined doc or separate short checklists for Procurement and Legal?

Cheers,

Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0128

Attachment: PO_Template_Hyperscale.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T08:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing discovery / private offer path — ops checklist

Aditya — quick ops notes based on AWS Marketplace private offer experience:  

- Buyer approvals: AWS requires the buyer to accept the private offer in their AWS console. On our side, we need: Seller private offer id, SKU, unit of measure, price per unit, term length, and the buyer AWS account ID (12-digit).
- Billing cadence: Marketplace supports Monthly/Annual. If Hyperscale wants to use its PO process, have procurement include the Marketplace offer id on the PO to avoid duplicate invoicing.
- Term length nuance: For 36m locked pricing, we need an explicit non-priced escalation clause in the SOW for major infra cost deltas. Finance also prefers 36m deals to route through legal earlier (due to revenue recognition complexity).
- Approval matrix: suggest this internal routing: AE (Aditya) -> Sales Ops (Vanessa) -> Legal -> Finance -> AWS AM -> Buyer Procurement -> Buyer Legal -> Buyer CFO. Add AM earlier if buyer asks for co-sell or reseller credits.

I drafted a one-page operator checklist (internal) that includes the exact AWS Private Offer metadata fields and DocuSign links we typically include. Will attach it to the shared drive; for now I’m adding the short list to the thread.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Benitez <sara.benitez@hyperscale.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@hyperscale.com>, AWS Partner Manager <am-partner@amazon.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing discovery / private offer path

Thanks both — Procurement ran some numbers. Hyperscale is leaning toward a 24-month commitment to balance price protection and budget flexibility. Our expected committed ARR for the initial term is ~$420k (annualized), so pricing at the 18% discount band sounds reasonable.

Procurement requests two things before formalizing the PO:
1) A single-sheet matrix mapping 12/24/36 mo to list price, discounted price, billing cadence, and buyer-signed approval owner (we can fill the buyer owner column).
2) The exact Marketplace private-offer metadata fields we should reference on the PO (seller offer id / sku / term / price unit).

If you can deliver these by EOD 2026-10-05 we’ll try to route internal approvals the same week.

Best,
Sara
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Benitez <sara.benitez@hyperscale.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@hyperscale.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, AWS Partner Manager <am-partner@amazon.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing discovery / private offer path — proposal attached

Sara / Procurement —

Attached is the single-sheet term matrix and the minimum Private Offer metadata package you should put on the PO (aws-private-offer-link.txt includes the console draft link). Key callouts:

- Committed ARR ~420k maps to the 24m discount (18%). We set billing to Annual in Marketplace but we will invoice Net-30 monthly to match Hyperscale PO preferences; buyer must accept the Private Offer to bind the terms.
- Required buyer fields: Buyer AWS Account ID, Primary Billing Contact (name + email), PO reference (if using one), and acceptance by an assigned buyer admin.
- Timeline: Once buyer accepts in Marketplace, AWS forwards acceptance to Redwood and we trigger order creation. If you want DocuSign for internal signatures first we can stage the DocuSign link so Legal can sign before acceptance.

Link: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/proposal/xyz-priv-offer-12345  (see aws-private-offer-link.txt attachment)

Proposed next steps:
1) Hyperscale Procurement confirms PO reference + buyer account ID (reply to this thread).
2) We prepare the Private Offer in AWS and share the offer id for your PO.
3) You accept the Private Offer in your AWS console; Procurement attaches the PO referencing the offer id.

Let me know if you want me to involve our Legal early — Vanessa flagged revenue recognition for 24m deals but that’s usually straightforward here.

Thanks,
Aditya

Attachments: aws-private-offer-link.txt, Hyperscale_SOW_v1.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T09:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Marketplace private offer — final ops notes for RDW-5421

Aditya / Vanessa — forwarding a short ops checklist I saved in Ops Docs for buyer routing. Re: RDW-5421, items to confirm before we create the Private Offer:  

- Confirm buyer AWS account id (12 digits) and primary billing contact.
- Confirm acceptance method: direct accept in AWS console vs. DocuSign pre-approval. If DocuSign, attach completed signature to Marketplace order to speed finance.
- Confirm whether buyer requires an SLA exception (we have standard SLA in Marketplace listing; exceptions need legal approval).
- If co-sell requested, note AM must create the Marketplace Private Offer with co-sell flag and include Partner Sales Credits metadata. Co-sell often adds extra approval cycles on both sides — flag to AM early.

I dropped a quick internal checklist and the HubSpot deal link in the doc. Will create the Private Offer draft once we have buyer fields.

-Marissa
